selection.title: Plants emit ultrasonic popping sounds when stressed
selection.author: Emma Caton
selection.topic: plant acoustics, experimental evidence and scientific caution
selection.diversity_result: No exact source repeat; narrow topic not used in the preceding seven days; selection balances science interest with transferable evidence-reading skills rather than research-topic overfitting.

content_observations: Tomato and tobacco plants were tested under dehydration and stem-cutting conditions in a soundproof chamber and greenhouse.
Stressed plants produced 30-50 pops per hour and microphones detected them up to five metres away.
A machine-learning model distinguished stress conditions and plant types.
The page explicitly says intentional sound production is unsupported, the mechanism is unclear, and ecological responses remain open questions.
source_verification.accessibility_scope: Official article text was directly readable; embedded audio playback was not required or claimed.
